title: Volumes, PVs, PVCs and StorageClasses
summary: Container filesystems are temporary; here is how data survives.

steps.title: Volumes
body: A container's own filesystem is thrown away when it restarts. A **volume** is storage attached to the **pod**:
| Volume | Lives as long as | Use |
| `emptyDir` | the pod (survives container restarts) | scratch space, cache, sharing files between containers |
| `configMap` / `secret` | the object | config files |
| `hostPath` | the node | node agents only; dangerous for apps (ties you to one node, breaks isolation) |
| `persistentVolumeClaim` | independently of pods | databases, uploads: anything you must not lose |
```yaml
volumes:
- name: cache
emptyDir: { sizeLimit: 1Gi }
- name: data
persistentVolumeClaim: { claimName: postgres-data }

steps.prompt: Your app writes uploaded images to `/app/uploads` inside the container, with no volume. The pod is rescheduled after a node upgrade. What happens to the images?
options: They are gone: they were in the container's writable layer on the old node
They are copied to the new node by the kubelet
steps.explain: Use a PersistentVolumeClaim, or better for uploads, object storage (Blob Storage, S3) so any replica can read them.

steps.title: PV, PVC, StorageClass
body: ```text
you write                    cluster provides
| PVC postgres-data     | --> | PV pvc-3f2a... 20Gi RWO    | --> Azure Disk / EBS / NFS ...
|  10Gi, RWO, class ssd |bind | created by StorageClass ssd|
- A **PersistentVolume (PV)** is a piece of real storage in the cluster.
- A **PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)** is a pod's *request*: "10Gi, ReadWriteOnce, class `ssd`".
- A **StorageClass** describes a kind of storage and the provisioner that creates PVs **on demand** (dynamic provisioning). Most clusters have a default class.
Access modes: **RWO** ReadWriteOnce (one node at a time: block disks), **ROX** ReadOnlyMany, **RWX** ReadWriteMany (many nodes: NFS, Azure Files, EFS), **RWOP** ReadWriteOncePod.
`reclaimPolicy: Delete` (the usual default for dynamic classes) deletes the disk when the PVC is deleted; `Retain` keeps it for manual recovery.

steps.prompt: Match the access mode to the storage.
pairs: an Azure managed disk or AWS EBS volume attached to one node
an NFS share or Azure Files mounted by pods on many nodes
a pre-filled dataset many pods only read
exactly one pod may mount it read-write

steps.prompt: A Deployment with 3 replicas spread over 3 nodes mounts one PVC with access mode RWO backed by a cloud disk. What do you see?
options: One pod runs; the others are stuck in `ContainerCreating` with a Multi-Attach error because the disk can attach to only one node
The PVC is cloned three times
steps.explain: Either use RWX storage, or a StatefulSet with `volumeClaimTemplates` so each replica gets its own disk.

steps.prompt: You create a PVC asking for `storageClassName: fast-ssd`, but no such StorageClass exists. Fill in the STATUS column of `kubectl get pvc`.
code: NAME            STATUS    VOLUME   CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   AGE
steps.explain: No PV can be found or provisioned, so the claim waits. A pod using it is also `Pending` (*unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims*). `kubectl get storageclass` lists what exists.

steps.prompt: Complete the claim for 10 GiB of single-node storage from the default class.
steps.explain: Omitting `storageClassName` uses the default class. `Gi` is 2^30 bytes; `G` is 10^9.

steps.title: Bind claims to volumes
prompt: Write `Dictionary<string, string> Bind(List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> claims, List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> volumes)`.

For each claim **in order**, pick an unbound volume with the same `Class`, the same `Mode`, and `SizeGi >= claim.SizeGi`. If several fit, take the **smallest**; ties by name. Map claim name → volume name, or → `"Pending"` if none fits. Each volume binds at most once.
starter: Dictionary<string, string> Bind(List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> claims, List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> volumes)
solution: Dictionary<string, string> Bind(List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> claims, List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> volumes)
